public-site.evidence: Feature is feature-complete: all 10 sections render and function end-to-end (hero→services→booking→story→testimonials→events→providers→contact→footer). Data integration is solid; sections properly display whatever content is provided (services show prices, events filter past dates, testimonials display quotes, providers group by 5 categories). However, trust strip is hardcoded copy that should be configurable, and error handling for failed fetches is minimal. Code is professionally written with proper accessibility, responsive patterns, and correct use of Next.js/TypeScript, but some architectural decisions (hardcoded navigation, trust messaging) would be friction points if this were handed off or needed to scale.

admin-cms.evidence: The content editing part is feature-complete and functional — Chelsea could edit all 8 sections if she could log in. But authentication is critically broken: login redirects to a non-existent route, API calls lack JWT, and no middleware shown to protect pages. The code works but reads like scaffolded-in-a-hurry: extensive inline style manipulation (ImageUploader:56-62, AdminSidebar throughout), identical save logic copy-pasted across 8 pages, basic error handling. This is 'shipped to meet deadline' not 'proud of it.'

gaps: Heading hierarchy not implemented anywhere — claim includes 'proper heading hierarchy' but code has zero h1/h2/h3 markup. Would need to be verified in page components, but not in this feature.

Keywords hardcoded instead of dynamic — lines 35-39 have hardcoded keyword array ['assisted stretching', 'Buffalo NY', etc] while description on line 37 is dynamic from CMS. Keywords should be `settings.siteKeywords` or similar, not baked.

Site URL hardcoded to single client — line 108 has literal `'https://rohlaxwellness.com'` instead of `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` or `settings.siteUrl`. Won't work for multi-tenant (Phase 2 per CLAUDE.md).
Fallback geo coordinates hardcoded for one location — line 142 defaults to `42.97, -78.70` (Williamsville, NY). For multi-tenant, this will silently give wrong location for other clients.

Address parsing is fragile — line 118-120 splits by comma and assumes exactly 3 parts ['street', 'city', 'state zip']. Fails silently if format is '123 Main, Williamsville, NY 14221, USA' (4 parts) or missing commas.
Hours parsing has no error handling — line 91 regex is complex
if `contact.hours` has unexpected format, regex won't match and entry silently disappears. No logging or validation.
Google Maps URL parsing silently degrades — line 138 tries to extract coordinates from URL with regex
if format changed or URL absent, falls back to hardcoded location without logging failure.

No JSON-LD schema validation — schema is constructed and stringified but never validated against schema.org. No verification that output is valid for Google's Structured Data Testing Tool (mentioned in claim).
Potential invalid schema field — line 149-152 includes `founder` field, but LocalBusiness schema.org type doesn't have `founder`. Should verify against schema.org spec.

No SEO preview for user — claim targets 'Google' but ignores Chelsea (actual user). No dashboard component for her to preview schema, meta tags, OG preview before publishing. She can't validate what Google will see.
seo.evidence: Feature renders working JSON-LD schema and meta tags for single client (Rohlax), but is architecturally broken for multi-tenant use (hardcoded URLs, coordinates, keywords) and missing a claimed feature (heading hierarchy). Code is readable but has fragile parsing with no error handling or validation—it works until the input doesn't match assumptions, then fails silently.

events.evidence: Feature works end-to-end for valid data (upcoming events filter, sort, display, link) but has silent failures on edge cases: unmapped host types render as 'undefined', empty/invalid dates disappear without warning, and zero validation prevents Chelsea from catching mistakes before save. Admin editor lacks error handling and positive feedback, making it feel fragile. Code structure is sound (semantic functions, good layout) but lacks defensive programming (error boundaries, validation, loading states). suppressHydrationWarning suggests unresolved timezone or parsing issues rather than fixed. This would work for a launch but would break with real customer usage.

provider-directory.evidence: Feature has the UI shell but is critically incomplete. Public display works and admin editing is functional, but the core value hypothesis (provider referral attribution → visible ROI in first week) requires working analytics wiring that isn't shown. Admin form allows client to edit recommendations when spec requires Laney-only control. Most damaging: 'Book' button is 9px text—completely unusable on mobile. Data validation is absent (no guarantee booking_link exists, no URL validation). Without visible seed data, it's unclear if 8 providers actually exist. Reads as a first pass: structure is competent but doesn't deliver on the promise.

Booking component fails as fallback for 6 non-FF services. Code supports the feature claim but does not prove it — 'all 7 services' linked is unverified from content layer.

ai-agent.evidence: Feature works end-to-end for 4 of 8 sections (services, events, contact, settings) — Chelsea can chat to update hours/add events/manage services and see it work. But missing system prompt context for half the sections, no persistence endpoint, and weak error handling leave it incomplete. Code is intentional (not sloppy), validation is pre-storage, array guard is smart. Feels like an MVP that ships but needs hardening before second client.

client-dashboard.evidence: Dashboard is functionally complete and polished — all promised surfaces (overview, chat, site preview, content map, settings) are wired and work. UX details are thoughtful (data-driven greeting, completeness score, status indicators). Code is clean with proper TypeScript and component organization. However, delivery depends entirely on backend APIs working correctly (not shown here), and concrete gaps prevent higher scores: hardcoded demo URL breaks multi-tenant, undefined CSS animation, generic error messages, inefficient persistence, missing validation. This is production-ready for a single client but would need fixes before scaling to multiple clients.

gaps: middleware.ts has no subdomain extraction — no code parsing request.headers.host or nextUrl.hostname to extract tenant ID (e.g., 'chelsea' from 'chelsea.reb.studio'). Feature claim requires this.

middleware.ts lines 22-46 — Routes are protected by JWT auth alone. Same token works for all tenants. No tenant context attached to request, so API routes cannot scope data by client. Multi-tenant isolation is impossible without this.
Missing entirely — No tenant validation. Even if subdomain were extracted, middleware doesn't check that it maps to a known tenant or reject invalid subdomains.
Missing entirely — No Redis scoping code visible. Claim requires tenant-scoped keys (e.g., client:${tenantId}:*). Cannot verify this exists without seeing API routes or Redis layer.
Missing entirely — No tenant configuration. No TENANTS env var, no mapping of subdomains to client IDs, no known-tenant lookup.
middleware.ts is generic JWT auth, not multi-tenant routing. The claimed feature (subdomain routing + tenant isolation) is completely unbuilt. This is a prerequisite guard, not the feature itself.
deployment.evidence: This is authentication middleware masquerading as multi-tenant deployment. The actual feature — subdomain extraction, tenant ID routing, tenant-scoped data access — is completely unbuilt. The middleware compiles and protects routes, but Laney cannot serve multiple clients yet because there is no mechanism to distinguish which client made a request. The code that exists is competent auth, but it solves a prerequisite problem, not the stated feature.
